transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Smith (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Rivera (Elysium CISO), Carlos Mendes (Elysium Head of Platform), Aisha Khan (Elysium Legal), Devon Lee (Elysium Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through security and data handling, I'll hand over to Priya for the technical bits. (audio glitch) sorry, little echo there.
[00:25] Priya: hi all, Priya here. quick agenda: retention, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and the no-training-on-customer-data guarantee plus DPA language. we'll keep it conversational.
[00:45] Dr. Maya Rivera: thanks. our main worries are PII/PHI leakage in prompts, who can see logs, and whether using Redwood will mean our data is used to further train models.
[01:05] Priya: totally understood. short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to train models by default - we have a strict no-training-on-customer-data policy for customers on enterprise plans; that is documented in the DPA. that said, I may have to caveat: for hosted trial accounts we sometimes have opt-in telemetry for improvement but enterprise is opt-out by default.
[01:32] Carlos: can you write that down? Legal will want explicit clause. also, what about prompt retention - we don't want full transcripts stored beyond X days.
[01:45] Jordan: absolutely. our platform has configurable retention windows for both request/response logs and full transcripts. typical enterprise retention options are 30, 90, 365 days, or custom - and we support immediate deletion on request.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: immediate deletion on request means logs are purged from live storage, what about backups? snapshots?
[02:18] Priya: good question. backups are encrypted and have a separate retention policy; we can arrange shorter snapshot retention or point-in-time snapshot deletion as part of the engagement. we'll document that in the DPA and security addendum.
[02:35] Devon Lee: on KMS - who holds the keys? we require BYOK for PHI workloads if possible.
[02:45] Priya: we support external KMS and bring-your-own-key. you can manage keys in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we integrate via envelope encryption. Redwood supports customer-managed keys for encryption at-rest; logs and model artifacts can be encrypted with your keys.
[03:05] Dr. Maya Rivera: rotation? access controls? audit of key use?
[03:12] Priya: keys can be rotated per your KMS policies; we log key usage events and can stream audit logs to your SIEM. key access is limited to the smallest set of services - we can provide architecture diagrams on exactly where keys are used.
[03:32] Carlos: about RBAC and SSO - we need SCIM provisioning, SAML, and fine-grained roles for dev vs. ops vs. data-science.
[03:42] Jordan: Redwood has SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and role-based controls with custom roles. there is an admin console where you can restrict who can export transcripts, who can create API keys, and who can view billing.
[04:02] Aisha: can we disable transcript export for non-admins?
[04:08] Priya: yes, export controls are role-based. you can also redact or mask PII fields automatically with our redaction tooling - it's a configurable pipeline using regex / ML-based PII detection.
[04:28] Dr. Maya Rivera: is the PII redaction deterministic? we need guarantees for PHI handling. sometimes redaction misses compound phrases.
[04:38] Priya: we provide both heuristic (regex) and ML-based detectors. for PHI-critical flows we recommend pre-filtering in your client before sending or using an on-prem/private deployment where you can run stronger redaction. also we can run a validation job on sample data during PoC to tune detectors.
[04:58] Devon: logging - we need immutable audit logs for compliance and a way to export them to our Splunk. retention longer than 7 years in some regs - can you support export and long-term storage?
[05:12] Priya: audit logs can be routed to your S3/Cloud Storage or SIEM via streaming; Redwood's internal retention can be shorter, but you can export and archive indefinitely on your side. we keep an indelible audit trail for admin-level events; we can enable write-once export hooks.
[05:36] Jordan: to echo, for regulatory retention you should export to your long-term storage. we can provide signed logs and timestamping to help with tamper evidence.
[05:50] Dr. Maya Rivera: about training again - is there any scenario where prompts/responses could be used to improve base models without explicit consent?
[06:00] Priya: for enterprise customers under contract: no, Redwood will not use your prompts/responses to train models. we also provide a contractual clause in the DPA and can agree to technical controls (retention, deletion, and log suppression). the only exception historically has been aggregated telemetry for platform health on non-enterprise plans, but not customer contents.
[06:25] Carlos: are there any metadata fields that are kept longer that might indirectly reveal content? like embeddings or derived vectors?
[06:34] Priya: embeddings are treated as derived artifacts and follow the same retention rules; we can suppress persistent storage of embeddings for sensitive workloads. for highest assurance, use Private deployment or Dedicated with no persistent embedding storage.
[06:54] Aisha: DPA - can you send us an initial DPA and the SOC 2 Type II report?
[07:00] Jordan: yes, we'll send SOC 2 Type II report and a DPA draft after the call.
[07:05] Priya: quick note on data residency: hosted regions can be constrained - we have EU and US regions, and Dedicated/Private options for on-prem or VPC.
[07:18] Devon: we want all data to remain in our EU region for the PoC. can you provision that?
[07:24] Priya: yes, we can provision a VPC-hosted private environment in the EU region for the PoC. that will also let you control network egress and KMS.
[07:40] Dr. Maya Rivera: legal will want stronger language around deletion guarantees and proof of deletion. can you provide proof-of-deletion artifacts?
[07:50] Jordan: we can provide deletion logs and attestations; for Enterprise we can agree on deletion SLAs and provide audit artifacts showing deletion timestamps.
[08:05] Carlos: any third-party subprocessors we should know about?
[08:12] Priya: we use cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) as infrastructure subprocessors; model hosting may include third-party model vendors for certain curated models - we can provide the subprocessors list and exclude any that are unacceptable.
[08:28] Aisha: about legal - are there sanctions or export control concerns with model weights being transferred across borders for some inference variants?
[08:36] Priya: inference can be pinned to region; we avoid moving model weights across borders for private deployments if requested - that's part of the deployment constraints we document.
[08:50] Dr. Maya Rivera: logging access - who at Redwood can see raw prompts in production for troubleshooting?
[08:58] Priya: only a very limited set of engineers with just-in-time access can view raw prompts, and access events are logged and require customer approval for each session for enterprise accounts - it's part of the escalation and support playbook.
[09:18] Devon: can you redact PHI before it ever gets to Redwood? like client-side filters?
[09:24] Priya: yes, you can implement client-side pre-filtering; Redwood offers SDK hooks and reference code for client-side PII/PHI redaction. we can share the sample repo.
[09:38] Jordan: quick housekeeping - we'll attach a security questionnaire answer set, SOC 2 report, DPA, and architecture diagrams to the follow-up email.
[09:50] Carlos: timeline - if PoC is to start first week Jan, we need docs by EoY.
[09:58] Jordan: we'll prioritize.
[10:05] (cross-talk, mumbled)
[10:20] Priya: ok last topic, incident response - we have a public incident response playbook and SLA for notification times. we send notifications to pre-defined contacts and provide root cause analysis.
[10:40] Dr. Maya Rivera: RTO/RPO for data?
[10:45] Priya: for hosted plans RTO/RPO are documented; for Dedicated/Private we can negotiate specific RTO/RPO in the contract.
[11:00] Aisha: exportability - we need the ability to export all customer content and logs for e-discovery. can you provide a bulk export?
[11:10] Priya: yes, bulk export is supported via the admin API and can be pushed to your S3 bucket or transferred via secure link.
[11:22] Jordan: cool, sounds like we have alignment on most items. to recap - we'll send SOC 2, DPA, security questionnaire answers, KMS notes, architecture diagram, and provision a EU VPC PoC with BYOK.
[11:40] Dr. Maya Rivera: thanks, we'll review and get back with any redlines.
[11:48] Jordan: thanks everyone. end.

Notes on transcript: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache) and filler words preserved to reflect conversational flow.
